claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has a coarse-grained microstructure.
The as-cast alloy undergoes a martensitic phase transformation that produces its caloric effects.
The as-cast alloy has poor mechanical integrity and is prone to cracking.
HPT at approximately 5 GPa for five rotations followed by annealing near 450°C for 30 minutes will refine the alloy's microstructure.
The proposed treatment will create an ultrafine and homogeneous grain structure.
The proposed treatment will create a high density of high-angle grain boundaries.
The resulting grain-boundary structure will impede crack initiation and propagation.
HPT-induced grain refinement will increase the alloy's yield strength.
HPT-induced grain refinement will increase toughness by creating barriers to crack propagation.
Low-temperature annealing after HPT will relieve residual stresses.
The annealing treatment can relieve residual stresses without substantially perturbing the martensitic transformation responsible for the caloric response.
The treatment will improve compressive strength by 50–100% relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treatment will increase resistance to cracking relative to the as-cast alloy.
The treated alloy will preserve its large caloric response.
The caloric transition temperature will shift by less than 2°C under applied magnetic and pressure fields relative to the as-cast alloy.
The intervention will remain effective under cyclic magnetic and pressure fields from approximately -10°C to 100°C.
Annealing parameters that significantly alter the martensitic transformation will compromise the intervention's effectiveness.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe processing under ambient conditions during annealing, whereas the intervention specifies annealing at approximately 450°C.
